- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias and reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in the 3rd–5th period of forecast window.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, apply a sentiment-weighted correction: +0.5% per +0.1 sentiment unit, -0.5% per -0.1 sentiment unit.
